findings.where: First screen, the white address button 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com →' (the page's one action); also the 'Contact' nav item
findings.fault: The primary action does nothing when clicked. Its link goes to '#', not to a mailto: address, so a visitor who clicks the button stays on the same screen and no email opens. The 'Contact' nav item also goes to '#' when it could take the visitor to this address. The only way to write to Mark is to copy the address by hand.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who decides to get in touch. They click the one button on the page, nothing happens, and the site looks broken at the moment of contact. Getting in touch is the page's job under brand sheet §1.

findings.where: First screen, the row of outlined pills under the lead paragraph ('PPP Law', 'Infrastructure', 'Development banks', 'Governments', 'Risk allocation'), on desktop and on phone, where they sit directly above the action
findings.fault: These are static labels, but they look like filter chips or topic links. Each one draws its own rounded white outline and sits in a row like a tag bar. Clicking one does nothing. They also share the action's white-on-blue language and are placed right beside it, so the first screen seems to offer six controls instead of one.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for Mark's work on PPP law or risk allocation clicks 'PPP Law' expecting his articles on it, and nothing happens. They also have to work out which of the boxed items near the bottom is actually the way to reach him.

findings.where: Article specimen, the list bullets and the PDF link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the ‘Abundance’ Challenge'
findings.fault: On the article page, links show in two different looks. The PDF link is orange-red and underlined, while the palette says links are house blue and 'Play again' is blue. The list bullets also use that same orange-red, so the colour that marks a link also marks decoration. The palette claims 'four colours and no accent', but this orange appears anyway.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's articles, which is where Angélique will add links. They cannot learn one link colour for the site, and the bullets in a link's colour make plain list text look clickable.

findings.fault: This is a button that replays the animation on the page, but it wears a link's look (underlined blue text). The underline is the mark the page reserves for links that go somewhere.
findings.who_objects: Few visitors would notice. Someone reviewing the tile might expect it to open a new page instead of replaying the motion.
